title: C#/.NET backend developer, new grad (insurance)
jd:
Graduate Backend Developer (.NET) - Harborline Mutual Insurance, Bangkok

Harborline Mutual processes more than 2 million motor and health claims a year, and the systems behind those claims are written mostly in C# on .NET. We are looking for a graduate developer to join the Claims Platform team.

In this role you will build and maintain REST APIs in ASP.NET Core that our call-center agents, brokers and mobile app depend on. You will write and tune queries against SQL Server, some of them inside stored procedures that are older than you are. You will write unit tests with xUnit and take part in code review from your first week.

We expect you to know C# and .NET well enough to read an unfamiliar codebase, to be comfortable with relational databases and SQL, and to understand how an HTTP API is designed and versioned.

It would help if you have used Entity Framework Core, deployed anything to Microsoft Azure, or worked with Docker. Knowledge of the insurance domain is not required.

We offer a 12-month rotation program, mentoring, and a hybrid schedule (3 days in office).

To apply, send your CV and, if you have one, a link to a repository you are proud of.

title: Data science intern (Python, scikit-learn, SQL)
jd:
Lumen Grocer is hiring: Data Science Intern

Lumen Grocer runs 85 supermarkets and an app. Our data team owns everything from demand forecasting to the loyalty program, built on a warehouse of more than 12 million transactions a month.

Responsibilities:
  - Explore customer and basket data with Python (pandas) and SQL
  - Build and evaluate predictive models with scikit-learn, for example churn or next-basket prediction
  - Help design and read A/B tests for app promotions
  - Turn results into short write-ups and charts for business teams

Requirements:
  - Currently studying statistics, computer science, economics or similar
  - Python with pandas and scikit-learn
  - SQL (joins, window functions, CTEs)
  - Basic statistics: hypothesis testing, confidence intervals

Nice to have:
  - Experience with Airflow or another scheduler
  - Tableau or another BI tool
  - Any experiment design / A/B testing experience

Internship length is 4 months, starting May or June.

title: Hardware test technician, entry level
jd:
POSITION: Hardware Test Technician (Entry Level)
COMPANY: Kestrel Power Systems - Amata Nakhon plant

2. IPC-A-610 certification

title: Rust systems engineering intern
jd:
## Systems Engineering Intern (Rust) - Ironleaf Data

Ironleaf builds a time-series storage engine for factory sensor data. The write path is Rust, the query layer is moving from C++ to Rust, and our p99 ingest latency target is under 2 ms.

### What you'll do
- Work on the ingest and compaction code in Rust
- Profile hot paths with perf and flamegraphs and make them faster
- Write tests, including property-based and crash-recovery tests
- Help expose internal services over gRPC

### You should have
- Real Rust experience (a project you can walk us through)
- Comfort with Linux and the command line
- An understanding of memory, threads and concurrency
- Git

### Nice to have
- async Rust with Tokio
- gRPC / Protocol Buffers
- C or C++
- Any storage or database internals coursework

Duration: 5-6 months. Remote within Thailand is possible.

title: Product designer who codes, junior
jd:
Fernway Health - Junior Product Designer (design + front-end)

Fernway makes appointment and follow-up tools for small clinics. We're a team of 14 and our designers ship their own front-end changes, so this is not a hand-off-to-engineering job.

What the work looks like: you'll take a messy problem, like a patient missing a follow-up, talk to clinic staff about it, sketch and prototype in Figma, and then build the screen in HTML and CSS with an engineer reviewing your code. Sometimes you'll put together a quick Framer page for a launch.

You might be a fit if:
- You have a portfolio that shows how you got to a design, not only the final screens
- You're fluent in Figma, including components and auto layout

- You've run usability tests or interviews yourself

- JavaScript or React
- Framer
- Helping build or maintain a design system
- Accessibility know-how (WCAG)
